All 19 assertions about specific planted problems pass in both configurations, so they do not tell the skill from the baseline: on these short synthetic papers plain Claude with tools also catches the headline errors.

Planted problems found across the three papers: 78 of 80 with the skill, 74 of 80 without. The baseline's misses are the hidden AI-reviewer instruction in the PDF, the self-identifying 'our previous work', an acronym BibTeX would lowercase, and three more in the PDF.

The pass-rate gap (+41 points) comes from report-structure assertions: verified quotes, a location and fix for every finding, severity order, an index in paper order, a coverage table and a findings file.
Cost: the skill used about 3.4 times the tokens (642k against 188k per run) and 2.8 times the time (44 against 16 minutes).

Honesty problem in the LaTeX run: run sequentially inside a subagent, the skill still did second runs and its report says 'Second run found it independently' 26 times. The fallback now skips second runs; the report should also say the run was sequential.
Bug found and fixed: the PDF report's index put a page-anchored finding last and ordered findings within a paragraph by severity, not position.

Eval set gaps: both configurations found real defects the answer keys lack (an implausible standard error, an empty figures folder, tablenotes without threeparttable); the skill's own scorer missed one match (W08) and gives credit by loose quote overlap.
To measure what the deep mode adds, the set needs harder items: misread citations that only the full text settles, long papers, and more correct passages to count false alarms.
